title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 2 — English | Paragraph Writing
description: Subject-wise test on Paragraph Writing (English) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 2. 40Q.
subject: maha2-english

questions.question: What is a paragraph?

options.explanation: A paragraph consists of more than one word.

options.text: A group of words that makes no sense
options.explanation: A paragraph should make sense and have a clear idea.

options.text: A group of sentences that talk about one main idea
options.explanation: This is the correct definition of a paragraph.

options.text: A very long story with many different ideas
options.explanation: A paragraph focuses on one main idea, not multiple ideas.

questions.explanation: A paragraph is a group of sentences that all relate to a single main topic or idea.
questions.hint: Think about how sentences are grouped together.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which of these sentences would NOT fit in a paragraph about 'My Favourite Toy'?

options.text: I have a blue toy car.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of a favourite toy.

options.text: I play with it every day.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of a favourite toy.

options.text: It has big wheels and goes fast.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of a favourite toy.
This sentence is unrelated to the topic of a favourite toy.

questions.explanation: A paragraph about 'My Favourite Toy' should only include sentences related to the toy.
questions.hint: Look for the sentence that is unrelated to toys.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: All the sentences in a good paragraph should talk about:

options.explanation: This is the correct characteristic of a good paragraph.
A paragraph should focus on one main idea, not many.
A paragraph consists of multiple sentences, not just one word.
A paragraph should discuss important and relevant ideas.

questions.explanation: A good paragraph focuses on a single main idea or topic.
questions.hint: Think about the unity of ideas in a paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which sentence would be the best *first* sentence for a paragraph about 'My Pet Dog'?

options.explanation: This sentence describes an action, not an introduction.
This sentence describes a habit, not an introduction.

options.text: I have a lovely pet dog named Buddy.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph.

options.text: Its tail wags when it is happy.
options.explanation: This sentence describes a characteristic, not an introduction.

questions.explanation: The first sentence of a paragraph should introduce the main idea clearly.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that introduces the pet dog.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Arrange the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph about 'My Best Friend': 1. We play together every evening. 2. Her name is Rina. 3. She is very kind and helpful. 4. I have a best friend.

options.explanation: This is the correct order: introduction, name, qualities, activity.
This order does not start with an introduction.
This order places the activity before the name and qualities.
This order does not start with an introduction.

questions.explanation: The logical flow is to first introduce the friend, then state her name, describe her qualities, and finally mention an activity they do together.
questions.hint: Start with the sentence that introduces the friend.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): A paragraph has many sentences. Reason (R): All sentences in a paragraph are about one main idea.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for why a paragraph has many sentences.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is the correct choice as both statements are true and R explains A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true as a paragraph has many sentences.

questions.explanation: A paragraph has many sentences (A is true), and the reason they are grouped is because they all contribute to one main idea (R is true and correctly explains A).
questions.hint: Consider why sentences are grouped together in a paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: What would be the best title for the paragraph about fruits?

options.explanation: This title is too specific as the paragraph talks about multiple fruits.
This title best covers the main topic of the paragraph.
This title is too general and does not specifically mention fruits.
This title focuses on a minor detail rather than the main topic.

questions.explanation: The paragraph discusses various fruits and their benefits, making 'Fruits' the most appropriate title.
questions.hint: Look for the main topic discussed in the paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which sentence would be the best concluding sentence for the paragraph about 'My Garden'?

options.explanation: This sentence is irrelevant to the topic of the garden.

options.text: I like to play with my friends.
options.explanation: This sentence does not relate to the garden.

options.text: My garden makes me very happy.
options.explanation: This sentence provides a fitting emotional conclusion about the garden.
This sentence is too specific and does not conclude the paragraph.

questions.explanation: A concluding sentence should summarize or give a final thought about the main topic. Option C provides a fitting emotional conclusion about the garden.
questions.hint: A concluding sentence should relate to the main idea of the paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which sentence in the paragraph about 'My School' does NOT fit well with the main idea?

options.text: My school is big and has many classrooms.
options.explanation: This sentence fits the main idea of describing the school.

options.text: There is a playground where we play games.
options.explanation: This sentence fits the main idea of describing the school's facilities.

options.text: We have many books in our library.
options.explanation: This sentence fits the main idea of describing the school's resources.

options.text: My friend Rahul lives near my school.
options.explanation: This sentence is about Rahul's residence, not a feature of the school.

questions.explanation: The main idea of the paragraph is about the school itself. The sentence about Rahul's residence is irrelevant to the main topic.
questions.hint: Identify the sentence that does not relate to the school's features or activities.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which group of sentences would make the BEST paragraph about 'A Rainy Day'?

options.text: I like to eat ice cream. My umbrella is red. The sky is blue today.
options.explanation: These sentences are unrelated to the theme of a rainy day.

options.text: The sun shines brightly. Birds sing in the morning. I go to school every day.
options.explanation: These sentences are unrelated to the theme of a rainy day.

options.text: The sky is dark and cloudy. Raindrops fall pitter-patter. I love to play in the rain with my paper boat.
options.explanation: These sentences are all related to the theme of a rainy day.

options.text: My cat is black. It sleeps on the sofa. I have a new book.
options.explanation: These sentences are unrelated to the theme of a rainy day.

questions.explanation: Option C contains sentences that are all related to the theme of a rainy day, describing the weather and an activity related to rain.
questions.hint: Look for sentences that are all connected to the theme of a rainy day.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which sentence would be the best start for a paragraph about your pet dog?

options.explanation: This sentence is too short and does not introduce the pet dog properly.
This sentence introduces the name but does not clearly state that it is about a pet dog.
This sentence introduces the topic but lacks a specific detail to make it engaging.

options.text: I have a lovely pet dog named Buddy.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces the topic and provides a specific detail (name), making it a strong opening.

questions.explanation: This sentence introduces the topic (pet dog) and gives a specific detail (name), making it a strong and engaging opening for a paragraph in Class 2. The other options are too short or less descriptive.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that introduces the pet dog and provides a specific detail.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Read the sentences below. Which sentence does NOT belong in a paragraph about 'My School'?

options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic 'My School'.

options.text: I like to play with my friends in the playground.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic 'My School'.

options.text: Our teachers teach us new things every day.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic 'My School'.

options.text: My mother cooks tasty food for me.
options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the topic 'My School'.

questions.explanation: Sentences A, B, and C all talk about different aspects of 'My School'. Sentence D is about 'My mother' and 'food', which is not related to the topic of 'My School'.
questions.hint: Identify the sentence that is unrelated to the topic 'My School'.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Choose the correct order to make a small paragraph: (1) It gives us light and keeps us warm. (2) The sun is a big star.

options.explanation: This order does not introduce the topic first.
This order introduces the topic first and then provides more information.
This option does not form a complete paragraph.
This option does not form a complete paragraph.

questions.explanation: The sentence 'The sun is a big star' introduces the topic, and 'It gives us light and keeps us warm' provides more information about the sun. This is the logical flow for a paragraph.
questions.hint: Start with an introduction sentence followed by a supporting sentence.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Read this short paragraph: 'Rohan loves to play cricket. He plays with his friends every evening in the park.' What is this paragraph mainly about?

options.explanation: The paragraph is not mainly about Rohan's friends.
The paragraph is not mainly about the park.
The paragraph is mainly about Rohan's love for cricket.
The paragraph is not mainly about evening time.

questions.explanation: The first sentence clearly states Rohan's love for cricket, and the second sentence gives details about when and where he plays cricket, reinforcing the main idea.
questions.hint: Identify the main idea by looking at the first sentence.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: What would be the best closing sentence for a paragraph about 'My Favourite Toy Car'?

options.text: I also have a blue toy car.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces another toy, which is not the focus of the paragraph.

options.text: My friend has a toy plane.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces another toy, which is not the focus of the paragraph.

options.text: It is my most favourite toy.
options.explanation: This sentence summarizes the feeling about the toy car and concludes the paragraph.
This sentence is too general and does not conclude the paragraph about the toy car.

questions.explanation: The paragraph describes the toy car. The sentence 'It is my most favourite toy' summarizes the feeling expressed and brings a good conclusion to the description of *that specific* toy car.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that summarizes the feeling about the toy car.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Arrange the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph: (1) We learn many new things there. (2) I go to school every day. (3) My teacher is very kind.

options.explanation: This order does not start with an introduction.
This order does not start with an introduction.
This order starts with an introduction, followed by a supporting sentence, and then a detail.
This order does not follow the logical flow.

questions.explanation: The most logical order is to first state 'I go to school every day' (introduction), then 'We learn many new things there' (what happens at school), and finally 'My teacher is very kind' (a detail about school).
questions.hint: Start with an introduction sentence, followed by a supporting sentence, and then a detail.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Complete the paragraph with the best sentence: 'Birds make nests on trees. They lay their eggs in the nests. ___________'

options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the sequence of events.
This sentence is unrelated to the sequence of events.

options.text: Baby birds hatch from these eggs.
options.explanation: This sentence logically follows the sequence of events.
This sentence repeats information already given.

questions.explanation: The paragraph talks about birds making nests and laying eggs. The most logical next step in this sequence is about what happens to the eggs, which is 'Baby birds hatch from these eggs.'
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that logically follows the sequence of events described.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** A good paragraph should only talk about one main idea. **Reason (R):** All sentences in a paragraph should be about different topics.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true, and Reason (R) is false.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true; a paragraph focuses on one main idea. Reason (R) is false; all sentences in a paragraph should be *about the same topic* or main idea, not different topics, to maintain coherence.
questions.hint: Understand the difference between a main idea and different topics.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Read the paragraph carefully: 'My garden has many colourful flowers. There are red roses, yellow sunflowers, and purple lilies. Bees and butterflies often visit my garden to collect nectar. It is a beautiful place to sit and relax.' Which of the following would be the best title for this paragraph?

options.explanation: This title only focuses on a part of the paragraph.
This title does not include all the details mentioned in the paragraph.
This title encompasses all the details mentioned in the paragraph.
This title only focuses on a part of the paragraph.

questions.explanation: The paragraph talks about the flowers, bees, butterflies, and relaxation, all within the context of 'My garden'. Therefore, 'My Beautiful Garden' is the most comprehensive and appropriate title.
questions.hint: Look for a title that encompasses all the details mentioned in the paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Read the paragraph: 'Monkeys are very clever animals. They live in trees and eat fruits. We often see them swinging from branch to branch.' Which sentence would be the *best* to add next to this paragraph?

options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the paragraph.

options.text: They can also use simple tools to get food.
options.explanation: This sentence supports the idea of monkeys being clever.

options.text: Trees are good for the environment.
options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the paragraph.
This sentence does not support the idea of monkeys being clever.

questions.explanation: The paragraph starts by calling monkeys 'clever animals' and describes their habits. Adding 'They can also use simple tools to get food' directly supports and expands on the idea of them being clever, maintaining the paragraph's focus and flow. Options A and C are off-topic, and D, while related, doesn't build on the 'clever' aspect as strongly.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that supports the idea of monkeys being clever.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which of these sentences best tells what a paragraph is about?

options.text: It is about many different things.
options.explanation: A paragraph usually discusses one main idea, not many different things.

options.text: It is usually about one main idea or topic.
options.explanation: This is correct because a paragraph focuses on a single main idea.
A paragraph can be about any topic, not just animals.

options.text: It is a very long story.
options.explanation: A paragraph is not necessarily a long story; it can be short and focused on one idea.

questions.explanation: A paragraph typically focuses on one main idea or topic, which is a foundational concept for paragraph writing.
questions.hint: Think about what a paragraph usually discusses.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Look at these sentences: 1. My dog loves to play. 2. He has soft brown fur. 3. His name is Buddy. Which is the best order to make a small paragraph about Buddy?

options.explanation: This order starts with an action, which is not the best way to introduce Buddy.
This order starts with a description, which is not the best way to introduce Buddy.
This order starts with the name, then describes Buddy, and finally mentions what he does.
This order starts with an action, which is not the best way to introduce Buddy.

questions.explanation: Starting with the name (3) introduces the topic, then describing him (2), and finally what he does (1) creates a logical flow for a simple paragraph.
questions.hint: Think about how you would introduce someone before describing them or their actions.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Complete the paragraph: I like to eat fruits. My favourite fruit is an apple. It is ______.

options.explanation: An apple is a fruit, not a vegetable.
This describes the apple in a way that fits the context of liking to eat it.
An apple is not an animal.
An apple is not made of paper.

questions.explanation: The sentence should describe the apple, fitting the context of eating and liking it. 'Sweet and crunchy' are common descriptions for an apple.
questions.hint: Think about how an apple tastes and feels when you eat it.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Read this short paragraph: 'My garden has many colourful flowers. Red roses, yellow marigolds, and pink lilies grow there. Butterflies often visit my garden.' Which sentence tells you the main idea of this paragraph?

options.explanation: This sentence provides a detail about the garden but does not introduce the main topic.

options.text: Red roses, yellow marigolds, and pink lilies grow there.
options.explanation: This sentence provides a detail about the flowers but does not introduce the main topic.

options.text: My garden has many colourful flowers.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces the main topic of the paragraph, which is the colourful flowers in the garden.
This sentence is not mentioned in the paragraph and does not introduce the main topic.

questions.explanation: This sentence introduces the topic of the paragraph, which is the colourful flowers in the garden. The other sentences provide details about this main idea.
questions.hint: Look for the sentence that introduces the topic of the paragraph.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Arrange the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph about a bird: 1. It flies high in the sky. 2. A little bird built a nest.

options.explanation: This order starts with the bird flying, which is not the best way to introduce the topic.
This order first introduces the bird building a nest and then describes its action of flying.

questions.explanation: The logical order is to first introduce the bird building a nest (2) and then describe its action of flying high in the sky (1).
questions.hint: Think about the sequence of events: first the bird builds a nest, then it flies.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: What is the correct order of the sentences to form a logical paragraph?

options.explanation: This order does not follow a logical sequence of events.
This order correctly follows the sequence of events.
This order does not follow a logical sequence of events.
This order does not follow a logical sequence of events.

questions.explanation: The logical sequence is to introduce the bird building a nest (2), state where the nest is (3), what happened in the nest (4), and finally what the bird does (1).
questions.hint: Think about the natural order of events related to a bird building a nest.
questions.subject: maha2-english

questions.question: Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph about the school bag?

options.text: I have a blue school bag.
options.explanation: This sentence is about the school bag and fits the paragraph.
This sentence is about the school bag and fits the paragraph.

questions.hint: Look for the sentence that talks about something unrelated to the school bag.

questions.question: What is the paragraph mainly describing?

options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

questions.question: Which sentence would fit best to complete the description of the little girl?

options.explanation: This sentence does not connect to the girl's appearance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complete sentence?

questions.hint: A complete sentence expresses a complete thought.

options.explanation: This is the correct logical sequence.

This sequence does not follow a logical order.

options.explanation: The reason does not explain the assertion.

questions.question: Which of these is a good topic for a paragraph?

questions.question: Which sentence shows the correct use of 'and'?

options.text: I like apples and mangoes and bananas.
